old_caption: The video captures a nighttime scene along a railway track. The camera is positioned low to the ground, providing a close-up view of the gravel bed alongside the tracks. The lighting is dim, primarily illuminated by a fixed light source, casting long shadows across the gravel. The railway tracks stretch into the distance, curving slightly to the left. On the right side of the frame, there is a pile of debris or logs, partially obscured by darkness but faintly lit by the fixed light source. The sky above is dark, suggesting it is either late evening or night. The overall atmosphere is quiet and somewhat eerie due to the low light and the stillness of the environment. The camera remains stationary throughout the sequence, with no movement of a vehicle or change in the shadows.
original_wisa_caption: The video captures a nighttime scene along a railway track. The camera is positioned low to the ground, providing a close-up view of the gravel bed alongside the tracks. The lighting is dim, primarily illuminated by the headlights of a vehicle moving towards the camera, casting long shadows across the gravel. The railway tracks stretch into the distance, curving slightly to the left. On the right side of the frame, there is a pile of debris or logs, partially obscured by darkness but faintly lit by the approaching vehicle's lights. The sky above is dark, suggesting it is either late evening or night. The overall atmosphere is quiet and somewhat eerie due to the low light and the stillness of the environment. As the vehicle approaches, its headlights become more prominent, illuminating the gravel and tracks ahead. The camera remains stationary throughout the sequence, focusing on the movement of the vehicle and the shadows it casts.
caption: The video captures a nighttime view beside a railway line, where the tracks run diagonally from the lower left toward a faintly glowing horizon. A gravel ballast path occupies the center, washed by a beam of light that throws two dark vertical shadow bands down its length. Dry grasses and a pile of flat debris sit at the right edge, while a single distant point-light marks the left horizon. The scene changes only subtly. The lit gravel band and shadow edges vary slightly in brightness and shape over time, and small handheld shake shifts the view a little, but the tracks, right-side debris, and grass tips remain broadly in place relative to one another. No train, person, or animal enters the view. The warm horizon glow, the track geometry, and the right-side vegetation remain persistently present throughout.

Audit this candidate caption against the actual chronological images, and correct factual errors.
This is a TEMPORALLY CROPPED EXCERPT from a longer video, not a complete event or a loop.
The first view may already be mid-action; the last view need not contain completion. Different
endpoints are normal, not physical errors. Do not add unseen causes, onset, stopping or outcomes.
An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless
the appropriate material/surface itself provides visible evidence. Do not infer a force or earlier
collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.
Compare several frames before asserting translation, rotation, direction, unchanged position or
camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.

Retain the WISA English narrative style, detail density and paragraph structure. Aim for the
provided original word count within 85%-115%, using genuinely visible details and process.
Do not add repetition, watermark/logo descriptions or atmospheric filler to reach a word count.
Do not shorten a rich caption into a terse technical checklist. Avoid annotation phrases such as
'this mid-segment', 'the excerpt', 'the frame', 'these images', 'observed evidence' in the caption.
This is a direct video description, not an analysis note. No mandatory beginning/end formula.
Complete every sentence. If accuracy requires a substantial length difference, explain it outside
the caption; do not fill missing context by imagination. Optional synonym edits are not needed.

Return JSON {"decision":"keep|edit", "issues":[{"quote":"exact span in candidate caption",
"problem":"concrete visual mismatch or unsupported assertion"}], "caption":"complete final caption",
"length_note":"empty unless required"}. Keep means unchanged caption and no issues. An edit
must actually correct the cited issue. This is a fallible automatic review, not proof of correctness.

draft_caption: The video captures a nighttime view beside a railway line, where the tracks run diagonally from the lower left toward a faintly glowing horizon. A gravel ballast path occupies the center, washed by a beam of light that throws two dark vertical shadow bands down its length. Dry grasses and a pile of flat debris sit at the right edge, while a single distant point-light marks the left horizon. The scene is not static. The entire frame drifts slowly sideways as a handheld camera translates along the path, so the bright grass tips and the debris pile shift position across the excerpt. The illuminated band on the gravel changes shape and slides relative to the background, indicating the light source and camera move together across the ground. Small frame-to-frame jitter accompanies this gentle motion. No train, person, or animal enters the view.
